source_title: LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman defends AI datacenters, has advice for tech companies
source_excerpt: As the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) data centres faces growing scrutiny across America, LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman is pushing back against critics, arguing that the massive wave of datacenter construction is keeping the US economy afloat. He said that it is the responsibility of the tech companies building the infrastructure to ensure there are no problems faced by nearby residents. Speaking on the Newcomer podcast recently, he gave advice to tech giants to address mounting neighbourhood pushback directly while pointing to the immediate macroeconomic boost.âMake sure the local community gets a sustainable benefit. Make sure noise, the environment, and everything else is taken care of. Make sure electricity prices stay the same or go down. And then allow the local community to say, âI want it, I donât want it,â and exercise their right to self-determination," he said, outlining clear conditions that developers must satisfy before moving forward with new builds.Escalating debate over infrastructure costsThe rush to construct facilities capable of training and running advanced AI models has ignited both political and social resistance across the US due to increased strain on power grids and drinking water supply.Data centres require tremendous amounts of power to run and cool high-density servers, sparking fears of strained regional power grids and higher residential utility bills. Similarly, heavy cooling requirements have raised persistent worries over the strain placed on local water supplies, alongside concerns over persistent facility noise.While the initial building phase drives demand for skilled trades like electricians and carpenters, completed datacenters require relatively few permanent operational workers on-site.
